title_en: Opinion of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Handling of Cases Involving Applications for Enforcement Supervision
keywords_en: Enforcement Objection; Handling of applications for supervision of enforcement cases
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Handling of Cases of Application for Supervision of Enforcement

Fa Fa [2023] No. 4

In order to further improve the procedures for handling cases of application for supervision of enforcement and to promote the correct and uniform application of law, these Opinions are formulated in accordance with the provisions of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and the requirements of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Further Improving the Mechanism for Restricting Enforcement Powers and Strengthening Enforcement Supervision, and in light of the actual circumstances of enforcement work.

Article 1 Where a party or a person not involved in the case is dissatisfied with an enforcement review ruling made by a people's court in accordance with Article 232 of the Civil Procedure Law and applies to the people's court at the next higher level for supervision of enforcement, the people's court shall place the case on file, unless otherwise provided by law, judicial interpretation, or these Opinions.

If an applicant, who should have raised an objection to enforcement in accordance with the law, fails to do so and directly applies to the people's court at the next higher level than the court against which the objection is raised for supervision of enforcement, the people's court shall inform the applicant to raise an objection to enforcement with the court against which the objection is raised or to apply for supervision of enforcement; if an applicant, who should have applied for a review in accordance with the law, fails to do so and directly applies to the people's court at the next higher level than the review court for supervision of enforcement, the people's court shall inform the applicant to apply for a review with the review court or to apply for supervision of enforcement.

If, in the course of handling enforcement-related petitions and letters, a people's court discovers that the petition request falls within the circumstances specified in the preceding two paragraphs, it shall handle the matter in accordance with the preceding two paragraphs.

Article 2 If an enforcement applicant believes that a people's court should have taken enforcement measures but failed to do so, and requests the enforcement court to take such measures, the people's court shall promptly review and handle the matter and generally shall not open a case for an objection to enforcement.

If the enforcement court fails to enforce within the statutory time limit, and the enforcement applicant, in accordance with Article 233 of the Civil Procedure Law, requests the people's court at the next higher level to take over the enforcement, order the lower people's court to enforce within a specified time limit, or designate another people's court to enforce, the case shall be placed on file and handled.

Article 3 Where a party is dissatisfied with an enforcement ruling and applies to a people's court for a review or for supervision of enforcement, in any of the following circumstances, the people's court shall, in an appropriate manner, explain the legal provisions or the legal remedies available to the party and generally shall not accept the application as a case of enforcement review or supervision of enforcement:

(1) In accordance with Article 234 of the Civil Procedure Law, the party is dissatisfied with a ruling on an objection raised by a person not involved in the case and either initiates proceedings under the trial supervision procedure or files a lawsuit with a people's court;

(2) In accordance with Article 32 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Modification or Addition of Parties in Civil Enforcement, the party is dissatisfied with a ruling on an application for modification or addition of parties and may file an action for objection to enforcement with a people's court;

(3) In accordance with Article 244 of the Civil Procedure Law, the arbitral award has been ruled by a people's court to be unenforceable, and the parties may either re-apply for arbitration or file a lawsuit with a people's court;

(4) In accordance with Article 20 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Enforcement of Notarized Creditor's Rights Documents, the notarized creditor's rights document has been ruled to be wholly or partially unenforceable, and the parties may file a lawsuit with a people's court;

(5) Other circumstances where the law or judicial interpretations provide that relief is not available through the enforcement review procedure.

Article 4 Where an applicant applies to a people's court for supervision of enforcement, the application shall not be accepted in any of the following circumstances:

(1) The application for supervision of enforcement is directed against an enforcement supervision ruling made by a people's court on an enforcement review ruling;

(2) The application for supervision of enforcement is submitted after the People's Procuratorate has decided not to issue a procuratorial recommendation in response to the applicant's application.

In the circumstance specified in item (1) of the preceding paragraph, the people's court shall inform the party that it may apply to the People's Procuratorate for a procuratorial recommendation, except where the enforcement supervision ruling was made as a result of a procuratorial recommendation issued by the People's Procuratorate.

Article 5 Where an applicant, dissatisfied with an enforcement review ruling, applies to a people's court for supervision of enforcement, the application shall be filed within six months after the enforcement review ruling becomes legally effective, by reference to Article 212 of the Civil Procedure Law.

Where an applicant applies to a people's court for supervision of enforcement because the time limit for raising an objection to enforcement or the time limit for applying for a review has expired, the application shall be filed within six months from the date on which the time limit for raising an objection or the time limit for applying for a review expires.

If an applicant applies to a people's court for supervision of enforcement after the expiration of the above time limits, the people's court shall not accept the application; if it has already been accepted, the review shall be terminated.

Article 6 Where an applicant is dissatisfied with an enforcement review ruling made by a High People's Court, the applicant shall apply to the original trial High People's Court for supervision of enforcement; if the applicant applies to the Supreme People's Court for supervision of enforcement, the Supreme People's Court shall accept the application in any of the following circumstances:

(1) The applicant has no objection to the basic facts found and the review procedures followed in the enforcement review ruling but believes that there is an error in the application of the law;

(2) The enforcement review ruling was made after discussion and decision by the Judicial Committee of the High People's Court.

Article 7 Where an application for supervision of enforcement is submitted to the Supreme People's Court, the application for supervision of enforcement, in addition to the matters that must be stated in accordance with the law, shall also state that the applicant has no objection to the basic facts found and the review procedures applied in the original ruling, and shall simultaneously specify the focal points of dispute concerning the legal issues involved in the case, and the reasons and basis for arguing that the ruling contains errors in the application of the law.

If the application for supervision of enforcement submitted by the applicant does not meet the requirements of the preceding paragraph, the Supreme People's Court shall provide guidance and clarification, and shall comprehensively inform the applicant in a one-time manner to make corrections within ten days; if the applicant fails to make corrections within the time limit without justifiable reasons, the application shall be treated as withdrawn.

Article 8 Where an enforcement review ruling made by a High People's Court is indeed erroneous in the application of the law and meets any of the following circumstances, the Supreme People's Court may open a case for supervision of enforcement:

(1) The case has significance for guiding the uniform application of law;

(2) There are major divergences in the application of law among similar cases that have become legally effective in the past three years, either within the Supreme People's Court or between different High People's Courts, and such divergences remain unresolved as of the time of case review;

(3) Other circumstances where the Supreme People's Court considers it appropriate to open a case for supervision of enforcement.

If the Supreme People's Court discovers that a legally effective enforcement ruling made by a local people's court at any level or a special people's court is indeed erroneous and meets any of the circumstances listed in the preceding paragraph, it may open a case for supervision.

Article 9 Where a case of application for supervision of enforcement submitted to the Supreme People's Court meets any of the following circumstances, the Supreme People's Court may decide that the original trial High People's Court shall review the case:

(1) The case may have circumstances such as unclear basic facts, illegal review procedures, or omission of objection requests;

(2) The application of law in the original enforcement review ruling may be erroneous, but the case does not have significance for guiding the uniform application of law.

Article 10 Where a High People's Court, after review, finds that the application of law in the original ruling is indeed erroneous and that the case meets any of the circumstances specified in items (1) and (2) of Article 8 of these Opinions, and considers that review by the Supreme People's Court is necessary, it may, after discussion and decision by its Judicial Committee, report to the Supreme People's Court for review.

After receiving the report submitted by the High People's Court in accordance with the preceding paragraph, if the Supreme People's Court considers it necessary to review the case itself, it shall place the case on file for review; if it considers it unnecessary, it shall not place the case on file and shall decide to assign the case to the High People's Court for review.

Article 11 The Supreme People's Court shall, within thirty days from the date of receiving the application for supervision of enforcement, decide whether to review the case itself or to assign it to the High People's Court that made the enforcement review ruling for review.

If the Supreme People's Court decides that the original trial High People's Court shall review the case, it shall, within ten days from the date of making the decision, transmit the application for supervision of enforcement and relevant materials to the original trial High People's Court for review and shall promptly notify the applicant.

Article 12 In addition to the methods for closing cases specified in Article 26 of the Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Filing and Closing of Enforcement Cases, cases of supervision of enforcement may also be closed by the following methods:

(1) Reversing the enforcement objection ruling and the enforcement review ruling and remanding the case to the objection court for a new review; or reversing the enforcement review ruling and remanding the case to the review court for a new review;

(2) Treating the application for supervision of enforcement as withdrawn;

(3) Terminating the review.

Article 13 When reviewing a case of supervision of enforcement, a people's court shall generally make an enforcement ruling, but if it does not uphold the request for a complaint, it may issue a notice of rejection based on the specific circumstances of the case.

Article 14 These Opinions shall take effect on February 1, 2023. After these Opinions take effect, if any previous opinions of the Supreme People's Court are inconsistent with these Opinions, these Opinions shall prevail.

For cases of application for supervision of enforcement accepted by the Supreme People's Court before the effective date of these Opinions, if the review has not been completed as of the effective date, the review shall continue.

January 19, 2023
